# Canonical graph reference sequences

These fixtures were generated by `scripts/generate_canonical_graph_fixtures.py`
with the Rust `canonical-training-graph` tool from slither_neuroevo commit
`8618f5f31965f389ef94e44d48513b139f913acd`. Each receipt records the independent
native source digest, target, compiler, canonical graph/sensor/equation identity,
and exact numeric file digests. The reference target is Windows x86_64 MSVC.
The reference math backend is `rust-scalar-v1`; live roundtrip qualification
also exercises `rust-sse2-v1`.

The six source graphs cover Input, tanh Dense/MLP, custom GRU/LSTM/RRU,
fan-out, explicitly ordered Concat, Split and reversed graph output ports.
All recurrent graphs include zero and nonzero initial states. Each sequence
contains 256 deliveries. Source nodes/edges are deliberately submitted in
reverse array order; Rust compiles the authoritative topology and packing.

`observations.f32`, `initial-state.f32`, `weights.f32`, `outputs.f32` and
`states.f32` use little-endian Float32. Native states include every next
continuation in step order. These are semantic parity fixtures with synthetic
observations, not gameplay datasets or imitation-quality evidence. No world,
authoritative run RNG or controller lease was used.

To generate a new fixture directory after a deliberate contract revision:

```powershell
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/generate_canonical_graph_fixtures.py --runner C:/path/to/canonical-training-graph.exe --output-directory new-fixtures
```

The generator refuses an existing destination. Review source/digest changes
and parity failures before replacing references; do not widen tolerances to
accept a revised recurrence or packing convention.
